reflexion_entries_to_archive: #s196-board-look: the portrait claim had sat 'unverified live' since S194 because injected screenshots never loaded atlases; driving REAL matches to POSTGAME both proved it and surfaced an unrelated overlap defect a fixture would never have produced (scores 301/298).

#s196-silent-drop: the S195 tree ruled the silent drop 'not reproduced here' because its blip was pc.close() (an SCTP abort the host hears); building a FAITHFUL silent drop (UDP blackhole) is what exposed the permanent split — a reproduction is only as good as its fidelity to the production failure.

#s196-host-only-tests: tower-fx's flare tests were all green and all on a HOST world; the joiner never saw a flare because the field it read is zeroed on the wire. Any render effect that reads sim state needs one host->snapshot->peer round-trip test, or it proves the host only.

#s196-click-offset: a long-standing 'click way to the left' bug lived for many sessions because every e2e ran at exactly 1920x1080, the one size where Pixi's per-axis mapping and the letterbox math agree; the owner's 'half screen / other monitors' was the whole diagnosis.

#s196-fix-rounds-chain: NONET took three fix rounds and EVERY one introduced a new MED (lost retries -> concurrent double-send -> claim-before-fold loss); only re-auditing each delta caught them. The final shape (one atomic batch) was the fix the auditor sketched, not the builder — when a round adds a defect, hand the next round the auditor's fix shape verbatim.

#s196-accounts-reuse: the owner's 'reuse what Legacy and CNC already built' turned a from-scratch design into a survey — and the survey surfaced two live security defects in OTHER projects (shared JWT key, open redirect). A read-only look at sibling projects is worth doing for its own sake; route what it finds to those projects, never fix across the boundary.

#s196-hosting-question: the owner's 'pay for a stronger server' was a reasonable guess from outside; the useful answer separated WHERE the game runs (host browser) from what was slow (a joiner backlog), and a measuring tree found the backlog before the research tree finished — evidence beat speculation by an hour.

#s196-team-art: a composed-art feature only pays off if the seating matches the art; the builder surfaced that a trio picture shows in ~1 of 6 lobbies — the kind of consequence that must reach the owner as a question, not be buried in a MINE list.

#s196-risen: a reported 'X doesn't work' turned out to be 'X works silently far from where he was looking' — the measured match (50 of 64 kills raised) settled it; the real gap is feedback, not mechanics.

#s196-render-perf: the S195 'leak' was mostly a census that counted Pixi texture SLOTS that never shrink; the measurement was the bug. One real leak hid behind it — measure the instrument before chasing the number.
